title: Managed Cloud Data Processing Platforms
contentDescription: Demonstrationed walkthrough of managed cloud data-processing services (e.g. EMR / Dataproc / Synapse Spark) covering cluster lifecycle, job submission, and cost/ops trade-offs versus self-managed Hadoop.
rationale: The prescribed syllabus covers distributed data-processing fundamentals but does not explicitly expose students to contemporary managed cloud platforms commonly used in industry.
expectedBenefit: Students can compare self-managed and managed platforms and relate MapReduce/Spark concepts to production cloud services.
sourceReference: Cloud managed analytics platforms vs Hadoop syllabus scope

title: Hands-on Big Data Pipeline Mini-Lab
contentDescription: End-to-end mini pipeline: ingest sample logs, transform with Spark/Pandas API, and visualize volume/velocity/variety characteristics beyond chalkboard definitions.
rationale: Gap analysis identified limited practical exposure in Module 1; this lab goes beyond prescribed theory to operationalize the 5 Vs.
expectedBenefit: Strengthens practical interpretation of big-data characteristics against real sample datasets.

title: Introduction to Vector Databases
contentDescription: Conceptual introduction to vector embeddings, ANN indexes, and when vector stores complement document databases like MongoDB in RAG-style analytics.
rationale: Syllabus covers MongoDB document storage but not vector retrieval patterns now common in AI-assisted analytics products.
expectedBenefit: Students connect NoSQL storage models to modern similarity search use-cases without replacing core MongoDB outcomes.

title: Lakehouse Architecture and Open Table Formats
contentDescription: Overview of lakehouse patterns and open table formats (Iceberg/Delta/Hudi) for governed analytics on object storage.
rationale: Industry gap notes Hadoop exposure alone under-prepares students for lakehouse stacks that supersede classic HDFS-centric teaching in many firms.
expectedBenefit: Links HDFS/MapReduce foundations to current lakehouse design choices.

title: Real-time Stream Processing with Kafka + Spark Structured Streaming
contentDescription: Demo of a streaming ingestion path: Kafka topic → Structured Streaming aggregation → sink, contrasting batch Hadoop jobs.
rationale: Prescribed modules emphasize batch-oriented processing; industry analytics increasingly require near-real-time pipelines.
expectedBenefit: Extends CO coverage toward latency-aware analytics design.

title: NoSQL Data Modeling Clinic for Analytics Workloads
contentDescription: Practical clinic on document modeling for analytics queries, indexing strategies, and aggregation pipeline patterns beyond textbook CRUD.
rationale: Assessment gap on MongoDB indicates students need structured practice applying modeling decisions to analytics queries.
expectedBenefit: Improves applied MongoDB competence tied to CO3 assessment readiness.

title: TLS 1.3 Handshake Deep Dive and Certificate Lifecycle
contentDescription: Protocol-level walkthrough of TLS 1.3 handshake, certificates, and common misconfigurations beyond textbook cipher lists.
rationale: Syllabus covers cryptographic primitives but rarely connects them to live TLS deployment practices used in production networks.
expectedBenefit: Students map crypto fundamentals to secure web/service communication.

title: Password Hashing: Argon2, bcrypt, and Breach Case Studies
contentDescription: Compare modern password KDFs and analyze breach case studies illustrating why MD5/SHA alone are insufficient for credential storage.
rationale: Industry gap on hash applications; enrichment focuses on credential storage practice beyond hash theory.
expectedBenefit: Connects hash properties to authentication system design.

title: OAuth 2.1 / OpenID Connect for API Security
contentDescription: Introduction to modern delegated authentication flows used by APIs and SPAs, including threat models (token leakage, CSRF).
rationale: Entity authentication in syllabus is classical; OAuth/OIDC dominate contemporary application auth.
expectedBenefit: Bridges theory of entity authentication to industry identity protocols.

title: Zero-Trust Network Access Concepts
contentDescription: Overview of zero-trust principles, micro-segmentation, and continuous verification versus perimeter-only models.
rationale: Prescribed network security often centers on firewalls/VPN; zero-trust reframes enterprise access control.
expectedBenefit: Prepares students for current enterprise security architectures.

title: Hands-on Packet Capture Threat Hunt Mini-Lab
contentDescription: Guided Wireshark exercise identifying suspicious flows and relating findings to confidentiality/integrity goals.
rationale: Assessment gap indicates need for practical evidence of security analysis skills beyond exams.
expectedBenefit: Builds applied packet-analysis competence.

title: Conceptual Modeling Workshop with Real Domain Case
contentDescription: Team ER modeling for a multi-entity campus domain with conflicting requirements and normalization trade-offs.
rationale: Practical gap in Module 1; workshop goes beyond textbook ER diagrams into contested real requirements.
expectedBenefit: Improves modeling judgment and stakeholder trade-off reasoning.

title: Query Optimization and EXPLAIN Plans in Practice
contentDescription: Use EXPLAIN/ANALYZE on sample schemas to show how indexes and join order affect relational algebra equivalents.
rationale: Industry expects graduates to reason about query cost; syllabus algebra rarely includes live optimizer evidence.
expectedBenefit: Links algebra operators to physical execution plans.

title: Transactional Integrity and Isolation Levels Mini-Lab
contentDescription: Demonstrate dirty/non-repeatable/phantom reads under different isolation levels with concurrent sessions.
rationale: Assessment gap on SQL/normalization; concurrency anomalies are rarely experienced hands-on in syllabus labs.
expectedBenefit: Makes ACID/isolation concrete through observation.

title: Introduction to Cloud Managed Relational Databases
contentDescription: Compare self-hosted RDBMS ops with managed services (backup, HA, read replicas) for application teams.
rationale: Syllabus focuses on DBMS internals; industry apps often consume managed SQL services.
expectedBenefit: Extends DBMS knowledge toward operational cloud choices.

title: Polyglot Persistence Decision Framework
contentDescription: Structured decision framework for choosing relational vs document vs key-value stores for sample product features.
rationale: Course emphasizes relational model; enrichment helps students avoid force-fitting SQL for every workload.
expectedBenefit: Builds architecture selection skill aligned to CO5/CO6 outcomes.

title: Wireshark Protocol Analysis Lab Beyond OSI Charts
contentDescription: Capture and annotate live frames mapping OSI/TCP-IP layers to observed headers.
rationale: Practical gap: students memorize models without inspecting real traffic.
expectedBenefit: Makes layered models observable.

title: Modern Access Media: Fiber, 5G RAN, and Campus Wi-Fi 6
contentDescription: Industry briefing comparing contemporary physical/access technologies to classic textbook media.
rationale: Syllabus physical-layer units emphasize classical media; campuses/industry now deploy Wi-Fi 6/5G/fiber.
expectedBenefit: Updates physical-layer intuition to current deployments.

title: Software-Defined Networking Concepts
contentDescription: Introduction to SDN control/data plane separation and OpenFlow-style switching control.
rationale: Switching in syllabus is classical; SDN is widely used in data-center networking.
expectedBenefit: Connects switching theory to programmable networks.

title: Campus Network Design Mini-Case
contentDescription: Design exercise for a multi-building LAN with VLANs and redundancy constraints.
rationale: Assessment gap suggests need for applied design evidence beyond theory tests.
expectedBenefit: Practices design trade-offs for LAN switching.

title: Network Security Hardening Checklist Seminar
contentDescription: Seminar on baseline hardening for edge/access networks as interdisciplinary enrichment.
rationale: Networking syllabus is protocol-centric; security hardening is an adjacent professional practice.
expectedBenefit: Builds secure-by-design awareness.

title: Regex Engine Internals: NFA Construction Demo
contentDescription: Live construction of NFAs from regular expressions and matching traces in a teaching tool.
rationale: Practical gap: automata theory is abstract without tool-assisted visualization.
expectedBenefit: Improves intuition for FA constructions.

title: Industrial Regex Safety and ReDoS Case Study
contentDescription: Case study on catastrophic backtracking and safe regex practices in production systems.
rationale: Industry uses regex widely; syllabus rarely covers denial-of-service risks of naive patterns.
expectedBenefit: Links theory of regular languages to secure engineering practice.

title: Parser Generators Briefing (ANTLR / yacc concepts)
contentDescription: Overview of how CFG/PDA theory underpins modern parser generators used in compilers/tools.
rationale: Syllabus proves CFG/PDA properties; enrichment shows tooling applications.
expectedBenefit: Motivates formal language theory through compiler tooling.

title: Computability Frontiers: Undecidability in Practice
contentDescription: Seminar connecting undecidable problems to real software limits (halting-related analyses, virus detection bounds).
rationale: Faculty enrichment situates undecidability proofs in software engineering limits.
expectedBenefit: Strengthens appreciation of theoretical boundaries.

title: Guided PDA Construction Studio
contentDescription: Studio building PDAs for curated languages with peer review of acceptance traces.
rationale: Assessment gap indicates need for more guided construction practice.
expectedBenefit: Increases accuracy on PDA constructions.

title: Parallel Profiling with Hardware Performance Counters
contentDescription: Demo of profiling parallel kernels using hardware counters / tools to diagnose speedup bottlenecks.
rationale: Practical gap: parallel theory without performance measurement.
expectedBenefit: Links Amdahl/scaling intuition to measured bottlenecks.

title: GPU Computing Primer with CUDA/OpenCL Concepts
contentDescription: Conceptual GPU execution model and memory hierarchy beyond CPU-centric parallel modules.
rationale: Industry massively parallel workloads are GPU-heavy; syllabus emphasis is often CPU/MPI.
expectedBenefit: Extends parallel thinking to accelerators.

title: Cloud HPC Job Submission Mini-Lab
contentDescription: Submit and monitor a small MPI job on a cloud/HPC queue, reviewing scripts and scaling logs.
rationale: Assessment gap on MPI; students need exposure to real job queues.
expectedBenefit: Operationalizes distributed memory programming.

title: OpenMP Tasking and NUMA Awareness Clinic
contentDescription: Advanced clinic on OpenMP tasking and NUMA locality effects.
rationale: Goes beyond basic OpenMP loops in syllabus toward locality-aware parallel design.
expectedBenefit: Improves performance-oriented parallel coding.

title: Parallel Computing in Data Centers: Guest Perspective
contentDescription: Guest/industry perspective on parallel frameworks used in production analytics/HPC.
rationale: Faculty enrichment connects academic parallel models to production frameworks.
expectedBenefit: Contextualizes course outcomes for careers.

title: International Business: Industry Toolchain Walkthrough
contentDescription: Demonstration of contemporary tools and workflows used in industry for International Business, highlighting practices not listed as prescribed syllabus topics.
rationale: Prescribed Module 1 content establishes foundations; industry toolchain exposure is outside the official unit list and addresses a documented practical gap.
expectedBenefit: Students relate core theory in International Business to tools they will encounter in internships and projects.

contentDescription: Faculty-curated briefing on an emerging technique/platform extending Module 2 of International Business without replacing prescribed outcomes.

title: Autograd and Computational Graphs Hands-on
contentDescription: Build tiny computational graphs and compare manual gradients to framework autograd.
rationale: Practical gap: perceptron math without modern autodiff tooling.
expectedBenefit: Bridges theory to framework practice.

title: Transfer Learning with Pretrained Vision Models
contentDescription: Demonstrationed fine-tuning of a pretrained CNN on a small custom dataset.
rationale: Industry rarely trains deep nets from scratch; syllabus focuses on from-scratch MLP training.
expectedBenefit: Aligns deep learning practice with industry transfer learning.

title: LLM Fine-Tuning Concepts (LoRA/QLoRA Overview)
contentDescription: Conceptual overview of parameter-efficient fine-tuning for large language models.
rationale: Emerging LLM tooling extends beyond classical DL regularization topics in syllabus.
expectedBenefit: Situates optimization/regularization knowledge in current AI practice.

title: MLOps Experiment Tracking Mini-Project
contentDescription: Track hyperparameters/metrics for a deep model with an experiment tracker.
rationale: Assessment gap; students need reproducible experiment habits.
expectedBenefit: Builds engineering discipline around DL experiments.

title: Responsible AI Failure Modes Seminar
contentDescription: Seminar on dataset bias, evaluation pitfalls, and deployment risk for deep models.
rationale: Ethics/risk is beyond technical syllabus units but essential enrichment.
expectedBenefit: Encourages responsible use of deep learning.

title: Linux Process Anatomy with /proc Exploration
contentDescription: Guided exploration of process state via /proc and system tools.
rationale: Practical gap: OS internals taught abstractly without live process inspection.
expectedBenefit: Makes process concepts concrete.

title: Scheduler Behavior under Load: Live Experiment
contentDescription: Run competing workloads and observe scheduling/latency effects.
rationale: Industry cares about latency under load; syllabus algorithms are often paper-only.
expectedBenefit: Connects scheduling theory to observed behavior.

title: Concurrency Bug Clinic (Deadlock/Race Case Studies)
contentDescription: Analyze classic concurrency bugs and repair strategies.
rationale: Assessment gap on synchronization needs applied bug analysis.
expectedBenefit: Improves deadlock/race reasoning.

title: Containers vs VMs: Isolation Models Briefing
contentDescription: Compare OS-level container isolation with hypervisor VMs.
rationale: Containers dominate deployment; syllabus isolation is classical process/VM focused.
expectedBenefit: Updates isolation knowledge for cloud-native ops.

title: Observability Stack Overview (logs/metrics/traces)
contentDescription: Faculty enrichment on how OS signals feed modern observability stacks.
rationale: Observability is beyond syllabus but connects OS concepts to SRE practice.
expectedBenefit: Professional systems literacy.

title: Agent Architectures in Modern Assistants
contentDescription: Compare classical agent PEAS models with tool-using LLM agent loops used in products.
rationale: Syllabus agents are classical; industry assistants use tool-calling agent patterns.
expectedBenefit: Updates agent thinking without discarding PEAS foundations.

title: Search Visualizer Lab (BFS/DFS/UCS Traces)
contentDescription: Interactive search visualizer lab producing traces for exam-style problems.
rationale: Industry/practical gap on search; visualization strengthens uninformed search mastery.
expectedBenefit: Improves correctness on search expansions.

title: A* Heuristic Design Clinic
contentDescription: Clinic designing admissible heuristics for grid/path domains and proving admissibility informally.
rationale: Assessment gap on informed search; clinic deepens heuristic design beyond textbook examples.
expectedBenefit: Strengthens heuristic reasoning for CO3.

title: Constraint Satisfaction in Scheduling Case
contentDescription: Apply CSP formulation to a timetable/scheduling case.
rationale: Moves CSP from abstract puzzles to an organizational scheduling case.
expectedBenefit: Shows practical CSP modeling.

title: AI Product Evaluation Rubric Workshop
contentDescription: Workshop creating evaluation rubrics for AI features (accuracy, latency, safety).
rationale: Faculty enrichment on evaluating AI systems beyond search/logic exams.
expectedBenefit: Builds critical evaluation skills.

title: Git and GitHub workflow for Java projects
contentDescription: Hands-on Git/GitHub workflow for Java coursework: branching, pull requests, .gitignore for Maven/Gradle, and collaborative review of OOP assignments.
rationale: The prescribed OOP-with-Java syllabus does not include professional source-control workflow used on every industry Java team.
expectedBenefit: Students can version Java labs and mini-projects with industry-standard GitHub practice.
expectedOutcome: A GitHub repository with a Java lab and a documented branch/PR workflow.

title: Unit testing with JUnit
contentDescription: Introduction to JUnit 5: assertions, test classes, parameterized tests, and testing exception paths for OOP assignments.
rationale: Prescribed Java labs rarely require automated tests; industry Java code is validated with JUnit.
expectedBenefit: Students can write unit tests for classes, methods, and exception handling.
expectedOutcome: A JUnit test suite covering core classes from a course mini-assignment.

title: Maven / Gradle basics
contentDescription: Build a small Java project with Maven or Gradle: dependencies, standard directory layout, and running tests from the build tool.
rationale: Syllabus compiles isolated programs; industry Java work is organized around Maven/Gradle builds.
expectedBenefit: Students can create, build, and test a multi-class Java project with a standard build tool.
expectedOutcome: A Maven or Gradle project that compiles and runs JUnit tests.

title: REST API development with Spring Boot introduction
contentDescription: Introductory Spring Boot REST controller exposing a simple OOP domain model (DTO, service, in-memory repository) beyond core Java syntax.
rationale: Industry Java roles expect familiarity with Spring Boot APIs; the syllabus stops at core OOP.
expectedBenefit: Students can map OOP classes to a minimal REST API.
expectedOutcome: A running Spring Boot service with at least two REST endpoints over a Java domain model.

title: Design patterns (Strategy, Factory, Observer)
contentDescription: Apply three GoF patterns to a Java case (payment strategy, object factory, event observers) using interfaces taught in Module 3.
rationale: Syllabus covers interfaces and inheritance but not named design patterns used in Java interviews and codebases.
expectedBenefit: Students can recognize and implement common OOP design patterns.
sourceReference: GoF patterns on Java OOP outcomes
expectedOutcome: A short Java implementation demonstrating Strategy, Factory, and Observer.

title: Java collections performance comparison
contentDescription: Measure ArrayList vs LinkedList vs HashMap vs TreeMap for insert/lookup/iterate workloads and relate results to Big-O intuition.
rationale: Collections APIs are used in labs without comparing performance characteristics needed for real systems.
expectedBenefit: Students can choose collection types based on measured cost, not only syntax.
expectedOutcome: A comparison table of collection operations with measured timings.

title: JDBC mini-project
contentDescription: Build a small JDBC CRUD application mapping OOP entities to relational tables (prepared statements, transactions, resource cleanup).
rationale: Core Java OOP does not include database access; JDBC is the standard next professional skill.
expectedBenefit: Students can persist Java objects with JDBC and explain SQL injection safety.
expectedOutcome: A JDBC CRUD mini-project with at least one transactional use case.

title: Debugging and profiling Java applications
contentDescription: Use an IDE debugger (breakpoints, watches) and a basic profiler/JFR overview to diagnose exceptions, leaks, and hot methods in a Java lab.
rationale: Students often debug with print statements; professional Java work uses debugger and profiler workflows.
expectedBenefit: Students can isolate defects and explain a simple performance hotspot.
expectedOutcome: A short debug/profile note capturing a breakpoint session and one hotspot.
